goal: A static Rust binary that reads what an agent produced and refuses the growth that should not be there, deleted or weakened tests, skips, stubs, swallowed errors, secrets, guardrail edits, dependency-direction violations, in milliseconds, with zero tokens, every finding as SARIF 2.1.0. `weed check` judges a diff and may block; `weed scan` judges the tree and never blocks; `weed guard` is the law in git through hooks; `weed bite` proves a test fails without its change. For maintainers drowning in agent-authored pull requests who need a deterministic gate before they read, for teams running agents on several harnesses who want one law, and for the garden's own fleets through pleach.

work.prompt:
You are a worker in a build loop. Make the checks below pass, honestly.
Nobody reviews your prose — only the verifier's verdict counts, so put all effort into the work itself.

## The goal
`weed scan` reads the repository as it is, not a diff, and names repo-state hygiene: a path, command, flag or symbol cited in the docs that no longer exists; a public symbol nothing references; a TODO older than the configured age; a dependency pin far behind the registry. It never blocks: exit 0 or 3 only, findings at warning level. tend2's hygiene loop is its first consumer, citing `weed scan --format sarif` as evidence; `docs/tend2-seam.md` is the proposal for that seam.

## Your environment
- You are at the repository root of an isolated git worktree. Work here directly.
- Leave your changes in the working tree; do not create branches, commit, or push.
- The loop file (docs/tend2/scan.tend2.html) is your full context — read it, including its narrative. It is READ-ONLY for you.

## Checks to close
- (code) with `[docs] commands` naming one command, a document citing that command, an unlisted command, a shell-only line and a destructive line, `weed scan` on a test-owned `PATH` runs only the listed command, only with `--help`, never the unlisted one, never a shell, and never an argument from the document, proven by the commands' own argv logs · evidence expected at: tests/scan_exec_bound.rs
- (code) a plain `weed scan` under a denied network exits 0 with findings, `weed scan --refresh-snapshot` under the same denial reports the registry unreachable, `src/` carries no `std::net`, `TcpStream` or HTTP client, and `weed rules` prints a `network` column that names R4's refresh as the only rule that reaches one and how · evidence expected at: tests/scan_offline.rs

## Definition of done — verify yourself before finishing
You are done when this exact command exits 0 (it is the gate the conductor will run):

    tend2 verify docs/tend2/scan.tend2.html --repo-root . --force --expect-payload 3faf14bbbd61 --runner 'bash scripts/check/run.sh {evidence}'

Run it yourself. If it does not exit 0, you are not done. Do not declare success in prose that a command disagrees with.

- 2026-09-05 R4 never reaches the network during `scan`; the snapshot is a committed file so the rule is reproducible in CI
- 2026-09-05 cape-town: tend2 is scan's first consumer and is on pollen; before R1 to R4 are finalised, ask tend2 which SARIF fields its hygiene loop reads (asked the same day; the answer goes here, and this loop is not dispatched until it lands or tend2 says it has no preference)
- 2026-09-05 `garden.json` lists the faces the binary answers and `tests/garden_manifest.rs` holds it equal to `weed --help`; this loop adds `scan` to the manifest's `faces` and to `SKILL.md`, or that test fails at its own gate
- 2026-09-05 cape-town: do not wait on tend2. Emit the minimal SARIF every consumer reads (ruleId, level, message.text, locations[0].physicalLocation.artifactLocation.uri, region.startLine) plus `properties.path` on each result for per-path aggregation; tend2's eventual answer is additive fields, never a change to those. Dispatched on that
- 2026-09-05 built by pleach node `scan` (claude/opus, codex audit) in one attempt, 45 minutes, landed by hand after `pleach land` met the rules-tests landing in `src/core/syntax.rs` and the fixtures README. The face reads the tree as it sits and leaves with 0 or 3; R1 resolves paths against the tree and commands against their own help through a new exec seam with a five-second deadline (`[docs] commands` names which); R2 exempts entry files, `main`, dunder names and runner prefixes; R3 asks git to blame only the files that carry a marker; R4 measures against `.weed/registry-snapshot.json` and `--refresh-snapshot` fetches through curl so the binary stays a judge. Every result carries `properties.path`. Conductor review found nothing to fix
- 2026-09-05 `garden.json` and `SKILL.md` now name `scan`; `docs/tend2-seam.md` shows tend2's hygiene loop citing `weed scan --format sarif` and proposes `weed check` in place of its `mock.ts`, with `scripts/check/docs-tend2-seam.sh` running the commands it shows
- 2026-09-06 cape-town, after milestone 5: two binding checks before calibration dispatches. R1 executes nothing outside `[docs] commands`, only with `--help`, never through a shell, never with an argument from the document, proven on a fixture with a test-owned PATH; and a plain `weed scan` is offline, proven under a denied network, with `weed rules` naming which rules may reach the network and how. Shaped as the two checks above

## Rules
- Write the failing test first where it does not exist; then make it pass.
- You must not edit the loop file — check states belong to the verifier.
- You must not weaken, skip, or mock the unit under test to force a green; mocked-unit evidence is detected and refused.
- Solve the CLASS of problem the claim names, not the test's example inputs. Hardcoding fixture strings, phrases, or patterns from the check or its tests into source (lookup tables, regex lists, phrase maps) is refused work even when the test goes green — it is an answer key, not a product.
- If the claim cannot be met generically with what you have, that is a real finding: write BLOCKED.md naming the missing capability (a model, a library, a redesign, a split of the check into honest tiers) instead of faking generality.
- Production quality only: no stubs, no TODOs, no placeholder implementations; match the style of the surrounding code.
- Probe/scratch files (toolchain checks, experiments) go in `.loop-scratch/` only — it is never collected; scratch files elsewhere pollute the delivery.
- If you are genuinely blocked, write BLOCKED.md at the repo root — what you tried, what stopped you, what a fix needs. An honest BLOCKED.md is a good outcome; a faked green is the worst possible one.
